Row.Text:
Europe, the Mediterranean and Africa above the Equator, at 112x98, 128x112 or 144x126. Three maps: Distant Lands (Africa, Scandinavia and Iceland across the water), One Landmass (the same geography with nothing distant), and a Variant kept apart so it can be reshaped without touching the originals.
EVERY CIVILIZATION OF EVERY AGE HAS A TRUE START. Pick the one that begins where you want your empire to end up. Civilization VII 1.5 added Gaul, England and Babylon, and they sit exactly where they belong, so the British line can now be played from where it actually happened: begin as Gaul on Lake Geneva, become England on the Thames, and end as Great Britain or America. Everywhere the game leaves empty, a civilization still waits - begin as the Mississippians on the Thames, or as the Maya on the north European plain and become Prussia in Germany. Only one age is ever live, so the ages share their sites on purpose.
ANTIQUITY - Rome (Rome), Gaul (Lausanne), Etruscans (Populonia), Greece (Thermaic Gulf), Byzantium (Constantinople), Carthage (Carthage), Egypt (Memphis), Assyria (Nineveh), Babylon (Babylon), Persia (Susa), Aksum (Axum), Mississippian (London), Heian (Dublin), Maurya (Madrid), Han (Kyiv), Maya (Berlin), Khmer (Bucharest), Silla (Ankara), Tonga (Syracuse).
EXPLORATION - England (London), Byzantium (Constantinople), Etruscans (Populonia), Tuscany (Florence), Bulgaria (Veliko Tarnovo), Spain (Madrid), Norman (Rouen), Abbasid (Baghdad), Iceland (Reykjavik), Mongolia (Sarai on the lower Volga), Songhai (Gao), Pirate Republic (Algiers), Sengoku (Copenhagen), Majapahit (Dublin), Chola (Lisbon), Goryeo (Athens), Dai Viet (Alexandria), Inca (Tbilisi), Hawaii (Syracuse), Shawnee (Warsaw), Ming (Moscow).
MODERN - Great Britain (London), America (Dublin), French Empire (Paris), Prussia (Berlin), Russia (Moscow), Ottomans (Ankara), Qajar (Tehran), Byzantium (Constantinople), Etruscans (Populonia), Mexico (Seville), Joseon (Athens), Meiji (Uppsala), Qing (Vienna), Siam (Naples), Mughal (Budapest), Nepal (Tbilisi), Buganda (Gondar).
Civilizations with no historical business in Europe are placed by terrain rather than by story, and matched to what their abilities care about where that applies: Inca and Nepal in the Caucasus, which unlock on mountain settlements; Hawaii on Sicily, which unlocks on island settlements; Buganda in the Ethiopian highlands, which unlocks on lakes.
Anyone left over settles a curated historical site, London and Dublin first, then Kyiv, Uppsala, Fez, Krakow, Trondheim, Copenhagen, Marrakesh and ninety more. Screenshots and details: https://marcobonechi.github.io/civ7mods/europe-mediterranean/
